law_name: New combat aircraft procurement programme (Air2030 / F-35A selection)
description: As head of the DDPS (2016-2018), Parmelin relaunched the fighter-jet procurement process after the 2014 Gripen referendum failure, structuring it so the final decision rested with the people. The 2020 popular vote narrowly approved a procurement-financing framework, and in 2021 the Federal Council selected the Lockheed Martin F-35A.
significance: Central to renewing the Swiss Air Force; the procurement later became politically contentious over the contractual price (see polemics).

law_name: Covid-19 economic support measures (short-time work / RHT and hardship-case aid)
description: As head of the EAER, Parmelin led the rollout of business-support measures during the Covid-19 pandemic, including a simplified short-time work (RHT) scheme extended to 18 months and a federal-cantonal hardship-case programme for firms suffering severe revenue losses.
significance: Among the largest economic-stabilisation interventions in modern Swiss history, supporting jobs and firms through the pandemic.

description: Parmelin championed the free-trade agreement with Indonesia, which included sustainability conditions on palm-oil tariff concessions. It was approved in the popular vote of 7 March 2021 after an opposition referendum.
significance: First Swiss free-trade agreement to be subject to a popular vote, and the first to link tariff concessions to sustainability requirements.

law_name: Termination of the Switzerland-EU institutional framework agreement negotiations
description: As President of the Confederation in 2021, Parmelin announced on 26 May 2021 the Federal Council's decision to end seven years of negotiations on the institutional framework agreement (accord-cadre) with the EU, citing unresolved differences on wage protection, EU citizens' rights and state aid.
significance: A major turning point in Swiss-EU relations that reset the bilateral track and led to later negotiations on a new package (Bilaterals III).
